passage:
**Business permit applications received by a town office, January to May 2025**

| Month | New | Renewal |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| January | 35 | 120 |
| February | 40 | 60 |
| March | 25 | 45 |
| April | 30 | 30 |
| May | 50 | 20 |
stem: In how many months did the office receive more new applications than renewals?
hints: Check each month one at a time. Compare the two numbers on the same row.
A month counts only if the New number is bigger than the Renewal number. Equal numbers do not count.
Go through all five rows, January to May, and count the months where New is the bigger number.

solution.methodName: Read the title and units, then find the row and column

steps.action: January: 35 new, 120 renewals. New is smaller, so January does not count.
February: 40 new, 60 renewals. New is smaller, so February does not count.
March: 25 new, 45 renewals. New is smaller, so March does not count.
April: 30 new, 30 renewals. They are equal, so April does not count.
steps.why: "More than" means bigger. 30 is not more than 30.

steps.action: May: 50 new, 20 renewals. New is bigger, so May counts.
Only May counts. The answer is 1 month.

trapNotes.2 months: This counts April too. In April, new applications and renewals are equal (30 and 30), so new is not more than renewals.
trapNotes.3 months: This counts the months where renewals are more than new applications (January, February and March). The question asks the opposite.
trapNotes.4 months: This counts the months where renewals are at least as many as new applications. The question asks when new applications are more.
